items.label: Figure 3

items.markdown: whether inhibiting its release could prevent the formation of intercellular connections. Upon co-exposure of neuronal and microglial cells to both α-Syn aggregates and BAI-1, cells failed to upregulate intercellular connections as observed in the presence of only α-Syn aggregates (Supplementary Fig. 6g–i). As a proof-of-concept supporting these findings, we next asked whether cytosolic nucleic acid alone could trigger intercellular connections. To test this, we treated

SH-SY5Y and HMC3 cells with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-737<sup>55</sup>, which induces limited MOMP and mtDNA release<sup>56,57</sup> in combination with the pan-caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh. Upon treatment, both neuronal and microglial cells had significantly increased intercellular connections at all the time points of treatment (6, 12, and 24 h) (Supplementary Fig. 7a–c), supporting the idea that mtDNA release is a key trigger for the formation of intercellular connections.
